# Why and With Whom

This part asks why an analysis should be reproducible at all. It
also asks what an analyst owes to the collaborators who depend on
the work. It is the first part of the first quarter, and it is
light on code. The chapters that follow supply the tools; these
chapters supply the reasons for using them. In the three-volume
edition, de-identification and the obligations an analyst owes to
the participants whose records make the work possible are covered
in the Compliance and Ethics part of Volume 3.

- @sec-why distinguishes methods, results, and inferential
  reproducibility, and names the check that makes each common
  failure loud.
- @sec-team-science runs the intake conversation, places an
  engagement on the collaboration spectrum, and settles authorship.

Each chapter opens with a short 'Skip ahead?' quiz. If the quiz at
the start of a chapter is easy, skip to the next chapter; if it is
not, the chapter is written for you.
